title: Getting On and Off: felszáll, leszáll

sections.title: A surface, not a space
sections.content: Hungarian treats a bus, tram or metro as a surface you climb onto, not a space you go into — that's why felszáll ("get on") uses -ra/-re, the same "onto" case from looking for a flat, and leszáll ("get off") uses -ról/-ről, "off of": Felszállok a buszra. ("I get on the bus.") Leszállok a következő megállónál. ("I get off at the next stop." — here megálló takes -nál/-nél, "at", since you're naming the stop, not the vehicle.)

items.spanish: Felszállok a villamosra a Blaha Lujza téren.
items.english: I get on the tram at Blaha Lujza Square.
I get off at the next stop.

sections.content: felszáll and leszáll are verbal-prefix pairs (fel- "up", le- "down") — in a question, the prefix and the verb can split apart: Hol szállsz le?, not Hol leszállsz?. You'll learn the full pattern later; for now just recognize both forms.
